transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-18
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Alvarez (Redwood AE); Priya Menon (Redwood SE); Dr. Maya Chen, Luis Gomez, Anika Rao (Cascade Therapeutics).

Summary: Quick hosted API walkthrough focused on chat/text generation basics: streaming, key generation params (temperature/top_p/max_tokens), retry behavior and idempotency, brief Console tour for routes and metrics, and a high-level mention of Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization. Customer asked about latency/cost tradeoffs and security (VPC, SOC2, KMS).

Topics: streaming responses, request params, retries/backoff, idempotency keys, hosted vs dedicated, VPC/private, security docs, pilot next steps.

--- Transcript (timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood. quick intros?
[00:08] Dr. Maya: hi im maya, cto at cascade therapeutics, we have luis engineering and anika on data. thanks for doing this.
[00:15] Jordan: awesome thanks. priya is our solutions engineer she'll run the demo, i'll cover pricing and next steps.
[00:20] Priya: hey all, hi, i'll share my screen in a second to show the hosted api flow, console, and a couple of examples around streaming and params. bear with me if the screen share lags a bit.
[00:35] Luis: quick note, our main concern is keeping inference latency under 300ms for chat suggestions, costs are also a factor but latency comes first.
[00:43] Jordan: got it. that's helpful. and what kind of throughput? concurrent users?
[00:47] Luis: right now it's a small cohort, maybe 50 concurrent but could grow to 500 over quarter depending on adoption.
[00:55] Anika: and data residency — we need eu-only data handling for some patient-derived datasets.
[01:02] Priya: noted. redwood has hosted regions and also a private deployment option for stricter residency; we'll include that in the security docs.
[01:10] Priya: ok pulling up the demo — first the basic chat call. so a hosted api request looks like POST /v1/chat/completions with a model param. you can stream tokens back by setting stream=true and we'll emit partial events for each chunk.
[01:30] Priya: (demo) here's an example payload: messages, temperature=0.2, top_p=0.9, max_tokens=128. with stream on you get chunked responses so you can render partial text client-side and reduce TTFB for the user.
[01:45] Dr. Maya: is streaming compatible with our websocket layer? we prefer websockets for UI.
[01:50] Priya: yes, we support streaming over http chunked and you can proxy via websocket; some customers prefer long-lived socket connections to receive streamed events. note sometimes partial tokens have punctuation split oddly — small artifacts when token boundaries happen.
[02:05] Jordan: casual note, streaming also helps perceived latency a lot since first token arrives quickly.
[02:12] Luis: how do you handle retries? we need idempotency so we don't double-charge or get duplicate responses.
[02:18] Priya: great question. recommended pattern: include an idempotency key for requests that have side effects. for simple generation, retries can be safe but if you do upserts downstream use idempotency. we also expose headers for rate-limit (X-RateLimit-Remaining) and suggest exponential backoff for 429s — we have a client SDK that handles standard retry jitter/backoff.
[02:38] Anika: what about partial results if a connection drops mid-stream?
[02:42] Priya: you'll typically get a partial chunk; you can attempt a resumed request but model state isn't stored unless you persist the convo tokens. an approach is to keep the conversation history client-side or in your storage and re-open with same messages. we also recommend KV cache for prefix caching — reduces token generation and latency.
[02:59] Dr. Maya: kv cache? can you explain quickly.
[03:02] Priya: sure, kv cache (sometimes transcribed as K-V cash haha) is the key-value cache for past key/value attention states — on repeated prefixes we can reuse those caches to avoid recomputing. that is more relevant for dedicated/private deployments but some hosted variants support session-level caches.
[03:20] Luis: ok interesting. what's the typical latency at 50 concurrent users using hosted?
[03:25] Priya: depends on model size; for mid-sized open models we see p50 around 80-150ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) on our optimized runtime; p95 varies. we can share the perf profiles per model. if you need strict 300ms p99, dedicated capacity or pinned smaller model variants can help.
[03:43] Jordan: i'll attach our model perf matrix with expected token throughput and cost per 1k tokens in the follow-up.
[03:49] Dr. Maya: costs — can you ballpark?
[03:51] Jordan: rough ranges in the pricing sheet. example: for text gen with an optimized 7B model, cost around $X per 1k tokens on hosted; dedicated discounts when you commit. i'll send a tailored estimate after we see your traffic profile.
[04:05] Priya: back to params — small changes in temperature and top_p can affect hallucinations vs creativity. for deterministic suggestions we recommend temp=0.0-0.2 and top_p around 0.7-0.95. max_tokens controls output length — set conservative limits for cost control.
[04:24] Anika: do you expose per-request metadata for tracing? we need token-level cost for analytics.
[04:29] Priya: yes console and api return token counts and cost estimates; Console has per-route breakdowns, and you can export logs/traces for cost analysis.
[04:37] Jordan: show quick look at Console — metrics, per-route latency, token cost, and request traces.
[04:45] Priya: (screen) this is the routes page — you can pin model versions, set rate-limits per route, toggle streaming, and configure fallback policies to alternate models when capacity is constrained.
[05:05] Luis: fallback — if you fallback to a smaller model, how do you keep output quality?
[05:09] Priya: we recommend semantic checks in your app; Redwood also supports automatic A/B rollouts and quality monitoring so you can set regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets. Optimize suggests quantization levels and batching profiles per workload to trade cost vs quality.
[05:26] Dr. Maya: security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs — do you have docs?
[05:31] Jordan: yes, Priya will share the security pack; we support SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS integrations, and audit logs. for data residency we have regional hosting and private deployment options.
[05:41] Priya: note for private deployments we do a customer-managed VPC option so keys never leave your network and HSM/KMS can be used for model encryption. we'll include the VPC checklist in the pack.
[05:53] Anika: encryption at rest in hosted?
[05:55] Priya: yes, hosted encrypts at rest and in transit; for more strict controls we suggest private with customer KMS.
[06:02] Luis: any known limitations around streaming for very long outputs?
[06:06] Priya: streaming is fine, but for very long outputs you may hit connection timeouts; we recommend chunking outputs and having the client re-request continuation using conversation context. also watch for token limits per request.
[06:18] Jordan: a quick note on retries again — our SDK supports idempotency keys and retry strategies. for 5xx we use retry with capped exponential backoff; for 429 we respect Retry-After header when present.
[06:30] Luis: ok good. question on rate-limiting — do you offer per-customer quotas?
[06:33] Priya: yes per-route quotas, per-api-key quotas; dedicated customers can reserve throughput and get SLA-backed latency targets.
[06:41] Dr. Maya: what's the onboarding timeline for a pilot?
[06:44] Jordan: usually 2-4 weeks: kickoff, access, small benchmark, then a short integration. private deployments take longer for infra setup. for hosted pilot we can get you keys and a sandbox within a few days.
[06:55] Anika: we can provide sample prompts and a 48-hour traffic trace — will that help?
[06:58] Priya: perfect, that will let us recommend model + batching settings. batching is important: Redwood Optimize can suggest ideal batch sizes and cache config to reduce unit cost.
[07:12] Jordan: i'll capture those action items now — i'll send pricing and perf docs; priya sends security pack and vpc checklist; luis and anika to provide sample prompts and traffic.
[07:20] Dr. Maya: any integrations with our infra — we run GCP europe-west1 primarily.
[07:24] Priya: we host in major cloud regions including europe-west; for strict residency we can do private deployment or region pinning.
[07:30] Luis: competitor question — how do you compare to openai in terms of cost and latency?
[07:34] Jordan: generalized: depending on model choice openai can be faster for some endpoints; Redwood focuses on predictable inference economics and gives tooling to tune cost/latency via batching, model variants, and dedicated capacity — plus the unified experience across hosted/dedicated/private.
[07:48] Anika: ok sounds good.
[07:50] Priya: quick demo of retries in SDK: show code snippet with idempotency key header and retry logic, and how to inspect response headers for rate-limits. (reads snippet) // small crosstalk, screen flicker
[08:20] Jordan: last bit — we'll include a small benchmark plan: 1) run small 1k request sample on hosted with your prompts, 2) evaluate p50/p95 latency and cost, 3) iterate with batching settings.
[08:35] Dr. Maya: agreed. when can we run that?
[08:38] Jordan: we can schedule the benchmark next week — aiming w/c 2026-09-27.
[08:45] Luis: fine with that. 
[08:48] Jordan: wrap up — recap of next steps and action items. thanks everyone.
[08:53] Dr. Maya: thanks. bye.
